neighbours.label: a collective surge sweeping through a population (a wave of protest, a tide of nationalism, a surge of joy through a crowd), as opposed to literal waves, tides and physical motion
fire: In the spring of 1848 a wave of revolution swept through the cities of Europe.
When the factory closed, a wave of despair settled over the whole valley.
During the 1990s a tide of optimism carried the new tech companies upward.
News of the victory sent a surge of joy through the waiting crowd.
By the 1920s a wave of prohibition laws had spread across the country.
The arrests set off a wave of strikes that swept the coal towns.
A ripple of excitement passed through the audience as the lights dimmed.
In the late 18th century a wave of abolitionist feeling grew in Britain.
quiet: In the spring of 1848 heavy rain flooded the cities of Europe.
When the factory closed, the workers moved away from the whole valley.
At high tide the water covered the rocks near the old pier.
The swimmer was knocked over by a big wave near the shore.
By the 1920s new laws had been passed in many of the states.
Radio waves travel through space at the speed of light.
The audience took their seats as the lights dimmed.
She waved goodbye to her friends from the train window.
